blocks.text: Narrow forest trail and lush, damp slopes in the Mashpi Reserve, Ecuador
Mashpi: a trail through ferns and trees above a misty valley

## About the trip

The next part of the trip takes you to the Mashpi Reserve. The road leads gradually down from the highlands towards the Pacific coast, through cloud forest and the area once inhabited by the Yumbo people. At Mashpi Lodge, the programme centres on the reserve itself, with daytime walks, time to observe forest life and evening outings.

You’ll spend the last four days in the Galápagos Islands. On Santa Cruz, you’ll see giant land tortoises and lava tunnels. You’ll then take boat trips to Bartolomé and either North Seymour or South Plaza. The programme includes walks through volcanic landscapes, opportunities to watch birds, sea lions and iguanas, and time for swimming and snorkelling.

The itinerary includes comfortable accommodation. In Quito, you’ll stay in a Royal Suite at the five-star Plaza Grande. At Mashpi Lodge, you’ll stay in a Wayra Room, and in the Galápagos, you’ll have an ocean view at the four-star Solymar.

## Highlights of the trip

The landscape changes several times in the course of this trip. In Quito, you’ll spend the day among squares, churches and highland views. The following day brings the open landscapes of the national park, Limpiopungo Lake and Cotopaxi, which rises to nearly 6,000 m. In Mashpi, the dry Andean air gives way to humid forest, dense vegetation and evening walks through the reserve.

The Galápagos portion is just as varied. On Santa Cruz, you’ll get to know the islands on land, among giant tortoises and lava tunnels. Bartolomé offers volcanic scenery and snorkelling off the shore. North Seymour is known for its bird and sea lion colonies, while the South Plaza outing combines a walk around the small island with a trip to Punta Carrión. Each day brings a different side of Ecuador into view.
